newsitem.title: MONACO: TENNIS-TRUYOL BANNED FOR A YEAR FOR DOPING.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-TRUYOL BANNED FOR A YEAR FOR DOPING.

text.p: Spaniard Ignacio Truyol on Tuesday became the first tennis player to be suspended for doping.

The ATP Tour, which controls most of the competitions in men's professional tennis, said in a statement that Truyol, 23, had "violated the tennis anti-doping rule for class I and II substances" and had been banned with immediate effect.
It said Truyol, ranked 127 in the world, would be banned for a year from all tennis and forfeit 192 singles ranking points.
The ATP said Truyol would also forfeit $39,985 in prize money earned since the Ostende challenger circuit tournament last July, suggesting that was when he failed a dope test.
It did not, however, say what substance Truyol had taken.
But it said a one-year penalty was applied in the case of class I products "which include steroids, masking agents and compounds".
Truyol's three-month ban for a first violation of class II substances, that include stimulants and narcotic analgesics, will run concurrently.

"We are disappointed that there has been a violation of the tennis anti-doping rule, but professonal tennis cannot tolerate the use of banned substances that may compromise the integrity of the competition," Mark Miles, chief executive of the ATP Tour, said.
It was the first time the ATP has found a player in violation of its anti-doping programme since it was introduced in 1993 and included random out-of-competition testing.

During the 1995 French Open, the International Tennis Federation (ITF), the governing body for the Grand Slam tournaments, announced that former world number one Mats Wilander and Karel Novacek had tested positive for cocaine.
The players denied having taken the drug and rejected the ITF's drugs testing procedures as unfair, appealing against a mandatory three months' suspension from all major tournaments.
